system_description.narrative_title: Democratic midterm sweep reshapes markets and risk perceptions
system_description.narrative_summary: Early results showing substantial Democratic gains in the 2026 midterms have driven rapid market repricing: equities rallied overall while risk-on/risk-off rotations hit specific sectors (data‑center/AI names fell, renewables and select cyclicals rose), the dollar and yields weakened, and oil prices swung on perceived shifts in foreign‑policy risk. Investors and analysts are recalibrating expectations for U.S. policy, regulation and energy strategy even as concurrent geopolitical flashpoints (notably Iran/Strait of Hormuz incidents) inject near‑term volatility into commodity and risk assets. The window captures an open system where electoral outcomes, market sentiment, sector positioning and geopolitics interact and feed back into each other over days to weeks.
system_description.scope: Inside the system: the 2026 U.S. midterm election outcomes and seat flips; immediate market responses (equities by sector, bonds/yields, FX, commodities like oil and gold); investor sentiment and short-term portfolio rotations; near-term policy expectations (energy, tech, foreign policy); contemporaneous geopolitical incidents that affect markets (e.g., Iran/Strait of Hormuz events).
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic system (the interaction of national politics, international geopolitics and global financial markets).
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. domestic politics and governance (legislation, oversight, executive-legislative interaction)
Global financial markets and investor risk appetite (asset allocation, sector rotation, flows)
Energy and commodities markets (oil, gas, renewables and strategic supply risk)
Technology and AI infrastructure sector (data-centers, semiconductors, cloud providers)

variables.name: Legislative majority balance
variables.description: The relative distribution of majority control across legislative chambers measured as a continuous balance of partisan control and its strength.

variables.name: Equity market level
variables.description: The aggregate valuation level of public equity markets measured by broad market indices and capitalization-weighted prices.

variables.name: Sector rotation intensity
variables.description: The pace and magnitude of portfolio reallocations across economic sectors, capturing shifts from one sector to another over short horizons.

variables.name: Aggregate bond yields
variables.description: The prevailing interest rate levels across fixed-income markets measured as a weighted summary of yields and yield-curve position.

variables.name: Currency value index
variables.description: The relative value of major currencies measured as an index reflecting broad foreign-exchange strength or weakness.

variables.name: Energy commodity price level
variables.description: The market price level for energy-related commodities measured as a continuous indicator of average energy cost.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The short-term realized and implied volatility of commodity prices, capturing uncertainty and dispersion in commodity markets.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: The aggregate willingness of investors to accept risk, measured by flows into riskier assets relative to safe assets and survey indicators.

variables.name: Policy uncertainty level
variables.description: The market-perceived uncertainty about future public policy changes, measured by news-based indices, option-implied measures and survey responses.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension intensity
variables.description: The current intensity of geopolitical friction and conflict risk as perceived by markets, measured continuously by incident frequency and severity indexes.

variables.name: Portfolio reallocation rate
variables.description: The flow rate of capital being moved between asset classes and regions, measured as net reallocations per unit time.

variables.name: Market liquidity
variables.description: The ease with which assets can be transacted without large price impact, measured by bid-ask spreads, depth and turnover metrics.

variables.name: Monetary policy expectations
variables.description: Market and agent expectations about the future stance of monetary policy, measured via forward rates, futures prices and survey instruments.

variables.name: Regulatory change expectations
variables.description: The anticipated likelihood and expected severity of regulatory interventions in key sectors, measured by market pricing, analyst surveys and rule-making signals.

variables.name: Energy supply risk
variables.description: The vulnerability of energy supply chains to disruption, measured as the probability-weighted risk of capacity loss and delivery interruptions.

variables.name: Corporate investment expectations
variables.description: Expected pace of corporate capital expenditures and investment activity, measured by capex plans, survey indicators and forward-looking guidance.

catalysts.title: Fed nominee Lisa Cook hearing
catalysts.description: Scheduled White House panel hearing on Fed nominee Lisa Cook that will clarify Fed governance and influence rate-path expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14.'

catalysts.title: Divided Congress gridlock
catalysts.description: Democratic sweep leaves Washington divided, raising the likelihood of legislative gridlock and fewer major policy shocks in coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Markets cheer Democratic win, betting divided Washington means fewer policy shocks'; 'Markets rally.'

catalysts.title: Sector rotation toward renewables and cyclicals
catalysts.description: Post-election repositioning: capital shifts away from AI/data‑center names into renewables, energy and cyclicals as market sentiment changes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI data-center stocks slide, renewables rally'; 'data center stocks tumble.'

catalysts.title: Middle East de‑escalation and oil supply recovery
catalysts.description: Markets price in a near-term easing of Middle East tensions and visible supply recovery, lowering oil-risk premia and commodity fear.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil sinks as midterms raise market hopes for Middle East solution'; 'JPMorgan, HSBC say oil supplies are recovering.'

catalysts.title: Potential impeachment proceedings
catalysts.description: Discussions and potential moves toward impeachment or related oversight actions that could raise political uncertainty and market nerves.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Impeachments, Iran and the presidency: what’s next after the midterms?'; 'Impeachments...' commentary.

catalysts.title: CVS corporate breakup execution
catalysts.description: Execution of CVS's announced breakup into separate pharmacy and insurance businesses, reshaping healthcare sector structure and expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'CVS to break up $117 billion business'; 'CVS Health to break up $102bn healthcare empire.'

catalysts.title: Post‑election bond yield decline
catalysts.description: Immediate market reaction and reassessment of rates following the Democratic sweep, driving short‑term declines in Treasury yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Treasury Yields Down Following Democrats Midterm Win'; 'Treasury Yields Fall on Election Results.'
